reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises by showing that annealing at 1200 °C for 8 h reduces the Laves phase, coarsens the HCP phase, and improves ductility in a V-Ti-Cr-Nb-Mo alloy. However, it provides no data on strength retention within a specific percentage or on impact-induced energy release, leaving the last two premises unsupported.
premises: Annealing at 1200 °C for 8 h can transform a triple-phase (BCC+HCP+Laves) V-Ti-Cr-Nb-Mo alloy into a dual-phase (BCC+HCP) structure.
This microstructural change reduces the brittle Laves phase and coarsens the HCP phase.
The resulting dual-phase structure improves ductility compared to the as-cast triple-phase state.
The strength remains high (within 10-15% reduction) after this annealing treatment.
The impact-induced energy release performance is unaffected by this microstructural change.
